sentences.text: Informal estimates place the length of this bird at nearly 30 centimeters, while the holotype indicates a length of 23.5 cm and a weight of 205 grams.
It possessed a tarsometatarsus measuring 46.8 millimeters in length and long legs with hooked claws adapted for perching and foraging on the ground or in shallow water.
Evidence suggests Neuquenornis lived in nesting colonies and buried its eggs in a behavior similar to megapodes.

The species was formally described by Chiappe and Calvo in 1994, with the holotype specimen cataloged as MUCPv-142 and housed in the collection of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales at the Universidad Nacional del Comahue in Neuquen, Argentina.
Chiappe and Calvo originally classified Neuquenornis in the family Avisauridae within the Enantiornithiformes.

Fossils were found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, which dates to the Santonian stage between 85 and 83 million years ago, restricting the time range for Neuquenornis to the Santonian, from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
Recent unpublished analyses suggest Neuquenornis may be more closely related to Concornis and Cathayornis than previously thought.
